name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{e}^{x+y}-x-y}{x+y}.
$$

 
The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form

$$
g(x,y)=C-x,
$$

where $C$ is a constant. What is $g(x,y)?$

Question 4
?

Consider the differential equation dydx=ex+y−x−yx+y. The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form g(x,y)=C−x, where C is a constant. What is g(x,y)?

a
e−x−y(x+y+1)
b
e−x−y
c
ex+y(x+y)
d
ex+y(1−x−y)
e
e−2x−2y
Submit
